## What the file does

`src/billing.ts` (311 lines) is the billing domain module. Five exports:

| Symbol | Lines | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `calculateRefundPreview` | 40–44 | Named like a pure calc; actually `await`s `saveRefundAudit` + `sendRefundEmail`, then returns `invoice.totalCents` unmodified |
| `generateInvoice` | 50–253 | The whole invoice pipeline in one body |
| `tax` | 257–268 | Country → tax rate → cents |
| `recommendUpgrade` | 272–305 | Four-deep nested plan-upgrade policy |
| `listRecentInvoices` | 307–310 | Stub — `TODO: replace with real DB query`, returns `[]` |

`generateInvoice` alone covers **nine** distinct responsibilities with no seams between them: id/metadata generation, per-plan line pricing (`pro` 5% / `team` 10% / `enterprise` 20%, with `addon_*` SKUs silently exempt), loyalty discount by account age, promo-code resolution, fraud-risk scoring, country tax, currency selection, PII-bearing `console.log` audit + metrics, email-body composition, and a fake retry loop that swallows errors.

Local types `User`, `InvoiceLine`, `Invoice` are declared in-file and **not exported** — anything that needs the invoice shape has to redeclare it.

- **`src/billing.test.ts`** — the only `likely_tests` entry, and it's a weak net. The scan flags both cases: *"renders the enterprise plan"* has **0 expect/assert calls**, and *"creates an invoice"* uses only weak matchers. Treat as near-zero coverage; `clues.test_gap` is **bottom-quartile**.
- **`src/routes/settings/billing.tsx`** — shares the `billing` domain token. Also carries its own `route_metadata_drift` finding (component `PricingPage`, `metadata.title: Plans`, `<title>: Subscription`).
- **`docs/billing.md`** — matches domain `billing`; is also one of the files in the `tenant`/`account` alias-drift group, so the vocabulary there may not match the code.
- **`src/date.ts`, `src/petty.ts`, `src/todo.ts`** — same-directory, weaker signal (score 0.2). `src/date.ts` matters most of these: it's the highest-risk file in the repo (8 direct clock reads, mixed UTC/local on one receiver, DST-naive `+ 86400000`), so it's the natural home if the clock ever gets injected.

Plus one the repo-wide scan surfaces that `context` doesn't:

- **`src/api/plan.ts`, `src/jobs/plan-sync.ts`, `src/ui/pricing.ts`** — the literal `"enterprise"` appears in all three *and* in `src/billing.ts:7`. If your edit touches plan-tier behaviour, these are the places the same policy is likely duplicated.

**The two that would actually bite an edit here:**

- **Logic in the Alibi (L39)** is the sharpest one. The comment states a real authorization rule — *only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves* — and the detector's evidence is that the terms `owner`, `plan`, `billing` **don't appear in the nearby code**. I confirmed that by reading: `calculateRefundPreview` performs **no** permission check at all. The rule exists only in prose. Any refund-path edit is working against an unenforced invariant.
- **False Identity (L40–44)**, same function. A `calculate*Preview` name that writes an audit row and sends a customer email. Anything that calls it speculatively — a preview UI, a retry, a loop — sends real email.

**Two duplications I found reading the file that no single finding names** (the scan sees the `"enterprise"` literal scatter, not these):

- Tax rates are written **twice** — inline at `generateInvoice:146–154` and again in `tax():258–266`. Identical ladders, no cross-reference. A rate change has to land in both.
- `daysSince` is computed identically at `L92` and `L273`, both off `Date.now()`.

**One likely-dead branch:** the promo block at `L105–126` reads `metadata.promo`, but `metadata` is constructed at `L58–64` and never gets a `promo` key. `promoCode` is always `""`, so all four promo branches are unreachable as written. Don't assume that code is live.

**Suppression to be aware of:** `commented_out_code::src/billing.ts::` is suppressed with the reason *"The legacy refund snippet is kept in comments for one more release; will be deleted in v0.3."* That's the dead block at `L33–37`. It's intentionally silenced, and `matches_current_finding: true` — so it's still there and still stale. Per the agent guidance: **do not copy logic out of it.**

## How I'd approach the edit

`agent_guidance` says *"Read the whole file before editing — propose splits in their own change."* I've read it, and I'll hold to the second half: I won't break up `generateInvoice` or the file as a drive-by. If a split is what you want, that's its own change with its own review.

For whatever the actual edit is, three constraints I'd work under:

1. **Don't add another `Date.now()`.** Seven already; thread a value in instead.
2. **Don't add a rate/tier table without checking the other copy** — tax has two homes, `"enterprise"` has four.
3. **`src/billing.test.ts` will not catch a regression.** If the edit touches pricing, tax, or refund behaviour, it needs a real assertion added in the same change — the existing tests assert nothing.
